title: Justice Department Announces Multi-Agency Trucking Industry Fraud Crackdown
dek: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a coordinated federal enforcement campaign against fraud in the trucking industry on August 31, 2026, involving eight U.S. Attorneys offices, DOT, DHS, FMCSA, and the White House Fraud Task Force. The effort targets illegal drivers, fraudulent commercial driver licenses, and unqualified training schools.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: In the past year and a half, USDOT removed 28,000 drivers from roads for failing to speak English, canceled over 30,000 illegally issued licenses to foreign drivers, and purged over 8,000 unqualified training schools from the FMCSA registry.
bottom_line: S. Attorneys offices may join the effort beyond the four named states.
body:
The U.S. Department of Justice announced a coordinated multi-agency enforcement campaign against fraud in the trucking industry on August 31, 2026, joining the Departments of Transportation and Homeland Security, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration, and the White House Fraud Task Force. Eight U.S. Attorneys offices participated in the announcement.
Some may be hauling drugs or weapons for international crimes networks." He framed the effort as dismantling fraud schemes harming American truckers, drivers, and community safety.
In July, FMCSA and DHS announced a partnership to further crack down on fraudulent and illegal practices in commercial driver license schools.
The announcement featured Marcus Coleman and his daughter Dalilah, who was critically injured in a 2024 crash involving an illegal alien driver, according to the Justice Department.
Secretary Sean P. Duffy of USDOT stated: "USDOT has spent the last year-and-a-half strengthening the rules of the road and removing dangerous foreign drivers from our trucking industry." Secretary Markwayne Mullin of DHS said: "Thanks to the recklessness of sanctuary politicians, there is a growing and alarming trend of illegal aliens being granted commercial driver's licenses. Many of them don't speak English or understand the rules of the road, and yet they're driving among us, endangering our loved ones."
White House Fraud Task Force Executive Director Scott Brady stated: "Americans have a right to feel safe on the roads their taxes pay for. Unfortunately, the previous administration disagreed and turned a blind eye to criminal enterprises that allowed drivers who couldn't pass a basic English test to obtain a commercial driver's license."
The effort includes formation of the Joint Task Force Crossroads of America, a multi-state task force designed to safeguard the nation's highway system and strengthen border security. It teams up the United States Attorney's Offices in Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, and Ohio with state and local enforcement, prosecutors, and federal partners including DOT, FMCSA, FBI, DEA, HSI, ICE, and ATF. Homeland Security Investigations Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon stated: "Criminals who exploit our nation's transportation systems through fraud and deception are not only breaking the law, they are putting the safety and security of the American public at risk."
FMCSA announced enforcement actions on the same day to stop fraudulent commercial driver license operations, though the Justice Department announcement does not detail the specific actions.
